movement_metrics.ideal_position_inference: Ideal next position = previous actual TCP position + command speed * time gap.
movement_metrics.actual_position: Actual next position = x, y, z from ur_tcp_pose_samples.csv.
movement_metrics.error_definition: Tracking error = distance between the actual next position and the ideal next position.

metric_1.name: Threshold-based Movement Accuracy
metric_1.formula: At a chosen millimetre limit, count samples inside the limit and divide by all samples.

metric_4.name: Recovery-aware Error Timeline
metric_4.formula: Start from 1, then subtract penalties for average error size, above-limit samples, and long repeated error runs.

critical_cases.explanation: Combined timing score is high because the robot is moving at the peak observed TCP speed. This pose is a useful physical-stability case even though RTT is not the highest.
RTT is in the tail at 303 ms, far above the 112 ms P95 benchmark. This is a typical network-risk pose where the operator may see stale state or delayed confirmation.
This is another high-RTT pose at 303 ms, but with lower motion lag. It separates communication risk from physical response risk.
A stop command appears while RTT is above P95. This is a safety-relevant case because the command intent is to halt or reduce motion.

error_marker_policy.tracking_error_source: nearest ideal-vs-actual TCP tracking error sample
error_marker_policy.warning_marker: orange when tracking error is above 10 mm
error_marker_policy.high_marker: red when tracking error is above 20 mm
error_marker_policy.current_frame_highlight: 3D replay frame and error badge turn red on high-error frames

replay_visualization.input_policy: uses computed metrics and local robot telemetry only; no visitor text input, file upload, or browser-side API key path

assessment.label: Responsive, with measurable network-to-motion tail risk
assessment.metric_definition: Physical Response Risk Window = Tail Timing Gap + command-to-motion P95
assessment.summary: The session is generally responsive, but the tail latency is important for trustworthy teleoperation. RTT P95 reaches 112 ms, command-delay P95 reaches 84 ms, and the largest RTT spike is 401 ms. This suggests the sim2real timing gap should be reported as a tail-risk measure, not only as an average latency.
assessment.motion_summary: The motion log shows 0.845 m of TCP travel, peak observed TCP speed of 777 mm/s, median operation interval of 20 ms, median command-to-motion response of 160 ms, and P95 command-to-motion response of 929 ms. The baseline TCP jitter P95 before active operation is 0.0618 mm, so the 0.5 mm response threshold is above the static noise floor.
assessment.trajectory_summary: Threshold-based Movement Accuracy reports 95.78% at the 10 mm tolerance using a one-step ideal trajectory inferred from speedl linear velocity commands. The Recovery-aware Error Timeline gives a score of 0.9518 because mean tracking error is 2.021 mm, P95 error is 8.015 mm, and the longest above-threshold episode lasts 9 samples.
